clue.text: Good looking, and one's time's engaged in cheating

indicators.note: engaged in means held inside, so these pieces sit within the other word

parts.note: dishy is informal British for attractive or good-looking
one's taken as ONES, the possessive's apostrophe dropped
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone attractive is caught up in a cheating scandal while a clock runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged in' puts ONES and T inside DISHY, between DISH and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheating is a form of untruthful, deceitful conduct, which is what the noun describes.

clue.text: Position in the East, say

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for East
to say something is to state it

explanation.surface: A remark about someone's standing somewhere in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like an example signal, but it is a verb giving STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Estate in the older sense is a rank or condition in life, a social standing.

clue.text: Regarding ideas, number one's cracking — of sound quality

indicators.note: cracking means breaking open, so the numeral splits the other word

parts.note: tonal means relating to tone, the quality of a sound
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone praises a top thinker's sound ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' puts I inside TONAL, after its T, making TIONAL to follow NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Notional describes something existing only as a concept or idea, not in reality.

clue.text: Not fully certain, stops further advances -then illegally takes

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: ups are rises or advances, as in ups and downs

indicators.note: not fully means the word is incomplete, its final letter cut off

parts.note: certain means sure

explanation.surface: An unsure person halts any further progress and then seizes power illegally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not fully' trims SURE to SUR, which 'stops' (plugs) UPS after its U.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp is to seize a throne or right wrongfully, without lawful authority.

clue.text: Father displays energy as a poet

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dad shows great vigour while posing as a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexander Pope was an English poet of the 18th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope, author of The Rape of the Lock, is an example of a poet.

clue.text: Makes known couples have left quietly

indicators.note: have left says a piece departs, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: pairs are couples
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly

explanation.surface: Gossip spreads after some couples slip away from a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To air an opinion or grievance is to voice it publicly, so airs means makes public.

clue.text: Start, and possibly spring in time to launch attack

parts.note: to open is to start
spring is an example of a season

explanation.surface: A military plan begins in spring, when the offensive is launched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' marks spring as one example of a season.
explanation.definitionFit: Open season is the period when hunting is allowed, and by extension a time when anyone may be attacked.

clue.text: One said not to forget marijuana plant

parts.note: the saying goes that an elephant never forgets
grass is slang for marijuana

explanation.surface: Someone who never forgets details a cannabis plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marijuana plant' reads as one thing; only 'plant' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephant grass is a tall tropical African grass, a plant used for fodder.

clue.text: Vitamin, the main one dispensed

indicators.note: dispensed like medicine, so the letters are made up afresh

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A pharmacist hands out the chief vitamin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispensed' rearranges THE MAIN plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: Thiamine is vitamin B1, found in grains and needed for metabolism.

clue.text: Sailor means to get high

definitions.meaning: one who reefs (shortens) sails, an old name for a midshipman
slang for a cannabis cigarette, a way of getting stoned

explanation.surface: A seaman finds a way to get high.
explanation.definitionFit: A midshipman who takes in sail is a reefer, and a joint smoked to get high is also called a reefer.

clue.text: For security reasons, lock up one after another, say

indicators.note: say means the words are spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: in turn means one after another, in sequence

explanation.surface: Prisoners are locked away one by one for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals that IN TURN sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern is to confine people such as enemy aliens, especially in wartime, as a security measure.

clue.text: Hasty, perhaps, to constrain anger, having returned in wild emotionalism

indicators.note: to constrain means to hold in, so one piece holds the other
perhaps says the word is one possible arrangement of its letters
having returned means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: Someone rash, holding in their rage, then snapping into a wild outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges HASTY to HYSTA; 'having returned' turns IRE into ERI; 'to constrain' puts ERI inside, after HYST.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysteria is uncontrolled emotion or excitement, an outburst of frenzied feeling.

clue.text: Gets going, to drop in shortly on Bill, perhaps

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the first piece above the second
shortly means cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to instil is to put in drop by drop
Bill Gates, founder of Microsoft, is one bearer of the surname

explanation.surface: Someone plans to pop in briefly on a person called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts INSTIL to INSTI; in a down clue 'on' sets it over GATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate something is to set it in motion, to start it off.

clue.text: Flogging sailors without a hint of mercy? An aid to their revival, perhaps

definitions.text: An aid to their revival, perhaps

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes round the letter

parts.note: flogging is slang for selling

indicators.note: a hint of gives just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: salts are old sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors flogged without mercy might need something to bring them round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: SELLING goes round M. 'Flogging' suggests whipping, but it means selling.
explanation.definitionFit: Smelling salts are a pungent preparation of ammonium carbonate used to bring a fainting person round.

clue.text: Turning up, I appeared fed -nevertheless become thin

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means read upwards, so the words go backwards

parts.note: I appeared means I came
fed means ate

explanation.surface: Someone arrives and eats, yet still grows thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' makes I CAME read EMACI, which goes above ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To emaciate is to waste away, growing abnormally lean from illness or hunger.

clue.text: Team to demolish extra food

parts.note: a side is a team
to dish is to ruin or destroy, as in dishing someone's chances

explanation.surface: A team sets about wolfing extra food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolish' suggests eating up, but here it is DISH in the sense of ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A side dish is an extra item served alongside a main course.

clue.text: Extremely giddy sailor circulating?

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extremes, the first and last letters

parts.note: a rating is a sailor below officer rank

explanation.surface: A dizzy sailor spins around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'giddy', G and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyrating is moving in circles or spirals, revolving round a centre.

clue.text: In short, this newspaper called for Democrat to tell the truth

indicators.note: called means spoken out, so the word gives a run of letters that sounds the same

parts.note: the Indy is the short name for The Independent, the paper this puzzle appeared in

explanation.surface: The newspaper briefly urged voters to back the Democrat, honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Independent is nicknamed the Indy; 'called' gives letters said the same way, IN-DEE, before D.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed, as a sentence adverb, means truly or in fact, admitting a point honestly.

clue.text: Nudist, ill-treated, has to undergo purification

indicators.note: has means the preceding words contain the letters within them

explanation.surface: A naturist, badly treated, has to go through a cleansing process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-treated' looks like an anagram signal, but the letters run on in nuDIST ILl.
explanation.definitionFit: To distil is to be purified by vaporising and condensing, the process used for spirits.

clue.text: Force ugly sisters not to include one

indicators.note: ugly signals the letters are reshaped, a nod to Cinderella's sisters
not to include means a letter is left out of the rearranged group

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Bullying the Ugly Sisters into leaving one person out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to include' drops I from SISTERS; 'ugly' rearranges the rest. Cinderella's two stepsisters are the Ugly Sisters of British pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is pressure or force, as on a beam under load.

clue.text: Keeping head out of source of light, turn and relax

indicators.note: keeping the head out means the opening letter is left off

parts.note: the sun is the source of daylight
to wind is to turn, as a key

explanation.surface: Someone sunbathes with their head in the shade, turning over to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping head out of' removes S from SUN, leaving UN before WIND.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwind is to relax after tension, like an uncoiling spring.

clue.text: Downy covering on ear, primarily, and part of neck

indicators.note: on in a down clue places one piece above the other

parts.note: nap is the soft raised pile on cloth

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the word gives its opening letter

explanation.surface: Soft fuzz grows on the ear and the back of the neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes E from 'ear'; in a down clue NAP sits on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The nape is the back of the neck.

clue.text: Civic dignitary plants tree in front of castle, say

indicators.note: in front of places this piece before the next one

parts.note: the alder is a tree of damp ground
a castle (rook) is one example of a man in chess

explanation.surface: A mayor plants a tree in front of a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'castle' suggests a building, but it is the chess piece, a chessman.
explanation.definitionFit: An alderman is a senior elected member of a borough or county council.

clue.text: Hoses patio following makeover-the best example

indicators.note: after a makeover things are rearranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: After a garden makeover, someone hoses down the patio to perfection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following makeover' rearranges the letters of HOSES PATIO.
explanation.definitionFit: An apotheosis is the perfect or highest form of something, its ultimate embodiment.

clue.text: Passage from dense epic to get through slowly

indicators.note: Passage from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An excerpt from a weighty poem drags on slowly.
